## Document: README.md (Overview)

# @actdim/ui-core

Shared UI foundation, theme system, design tokens, adaptive layout, and Dynstruct component conventions for Actdim applications.

## Overview
- **Theme Engine**: Semantic CSS design tokens, PostCSS build-time generator, runtime variable overrides (`themeRuntime`), and compile-time class validator (`tw()`).
- **Adaptive Layout**: Screen tiers (`compact`, `medium`, `expanded`), orientation detection, safe-area insets, and prioritized hardware Back-Stack navigation.
- **Adaptive Overlays**: `AdaptiveDialog`, `ActionSheet`, and `AdaptiveMenu` with unified `onClose` contracts and two-way bound `open` states.
- **AI Guidelines**: Comprehensive developer and AI agent conventions for Dynstruct + MsgMesh development.

## Documentation
- [Knowledge Base Index](docs/INDEX.md)
- [Frontend Coding Conventions](docs/topic--frontend-conventions.md)
- [Theme Tokens & tw() Helper](docs/topic--theme-tokens.md)
- [Adaptive Overlays Guide](docs/topic--adaptive-overlays.md)
- [Adaptive Layout & Back-Stack](docs/topic--adaptive-layout.md)

## Document: AGENTS.md (Agent Conventions & Protocol)

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-PROTOCOL root (managed by along-init - do not edit by hand) -->
# ALONG-PROTOCOL v4.6.0

This repo carries its own agent context, provider-agnostically. Follow it every session, whatever tool you are. This is the core; procedures (completion checklist, doc routing, merges, along-team, tool-use rules) live in `docs/topic--along-protocol.md` - pull the section you need via `/along-kb-search`. A gate's error message carries its detail.

## Where state lives
- **Nearest wins**: any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST for the area you work in. Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config. Only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject.
- **Read at session start** (not auto-loaded): `.along/ISSUES.md`, `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`, your issue `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md`; when relevant `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. They reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify named files/APIs/flags against the code.
- **Entities**: issues (`feat|bug|debt|task|docs|spike`), ADRs (`.along/DECISIONS/`, never edited - superseded), milestones, sessions. Keys `<type>--<slug>`, referenced by key, never by path; schemas in `docs/topic--domain-model.md`. Create them from intent unprompted (build/fix -> issue, blocked -> issue tagged `risk`, compare -> `spike` issue, release -> milestone).
- **Projections** (`ISSUES.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`) are compiled: on conflict take either side and re-run the sync.

## Anchor work to an issue
1. Find or create the issue with `status: in-progress`; `along start <slug>` binds this session.
2. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`, or `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after their explicit yes). Questions get read-only answers; 1-line typo/comment edits are exempt.
3. Commit via `/along-commit`: bound to the slug, no AI `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.
4. Finish with the completion checklist, ending in `along wrap <slug> --summary "..." (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)`.

## Gates
Runtime hooks enforce these where installed; elsewhere (`along doctor` shows the level) self-apply every one and use the `along` CLI instead of raw tools.
- [gate: require-active-issue] [gate: require-plan-approval] - no source edit without an in-progress issue and an approved plan.
- [gate: subproject-boundary] - a subproject's entities go in ITS `.along/`; cross-subproject work needs an issue in each, or a root umbrella with `parent:` children.
- [gate: workspace-containment] - read/write inside the workspace (plus temp); other roots need `allowed_roots`; never credential stores.
- [gate: projection-protection] - never hand-edit or hand-merge projections.
- [gate: commit-issue-binding] - every commit names the active issue.
- [gate: issue-lifecycle] [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection] - close via `along wrap` / `along issue done`; rename or supersede, never delete a referenced entity.
- [gate: doc-manual-lock] - `write_policy: manual` docs change only under a `docs--<slug>` issue.
- [gate: rule-pack-protection] - never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md` (`along rules attach` owns them).
- [gate: doc-routing-compliance] - ADR vs `README.md` vs `docs/topic--*.md` routing tree.
- [gate: untracked-exports] - dashboards and `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- [gate: cli_safety] - file content via file tools, never heredocs or `python -c`; no global installs.
- [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop] - an `along-team` blackboard holds you to its step loop.
- [gate: test_before_stop] [gate: wrap_before_stop] [gate: projection_sync_before_stop] - before stopping: tests run after your last edit, session wrapped, projections synced.
- [gate: unresolved_gate_denial] - a denied tool call is redone within the gate's rules or told to the user (`along gates ack`), never dropped silently; closing waits for their reply.
- Commit-time (`along lint`, pre-commit + CI): ASCII typography, fence languages, relative links, no `docs/` -> `.along/` links, Windows-safe names, no secrets, no stubs.
- Bypass is the user's call: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` after their reply; recorded in `along gates stats`.

## Judgment rules
- Ground facts in code, `README.md` and `docs/`; no generic placeholders. Query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole docs; update affected `docs/topic--*.md` after non-trivial changes.
- Use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw commands, with quiet flags. Review your diff and blast radius (`along graph-impact`).
- Never delete or truncate docs, comments or code unless told; no stubs; check `git diff --stat` after batch edits. Verify written files parse. Tests stay hermetic.
- Stay in scope: failures your issue did not cause (red at HEAD, untouched code) are reported and filed as an issue, never fixed under this one; never edit tests or fixtures to make them pass unless the issue is about them; bypass (`-n --reason`) only after the user's reply.
- Scope > 3 files, crossing subsystems or refactoring core engines: route to `along-team`; plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`.
- Treat the `along` CLI as a black box (`along <cmd> --help`, no engine source outside the Along repo); report its errors verbatim.
<!-- END ALONG-PROTOCOL -->

## Project specifics

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-RULES -->
See the following engineering guidelines:
- `[languages/typescript.md](.along/rules/languages/typescript.md)`
- `[platforms/web.md](.along/rules/platforms/web.md)`
<!-- END ALONG-RULES -->

- **Project**: `@actdim/ui-core` - Shared UI foundation, design tokens, theme runtime, adaptive layout, and overlay components for Actdim applications.
- **Dynstruct**: Component model for all UI elements with strict prop-less JSX in `view`.
- **MsgMesh**: Typed event bus for cross-component coordination, theme changes, and layout notifications.
- **Frontend Invariants**:
  - Multi-line `{ ... }` blocks for all control flow; `type` only - no `interface`, no `class`.
  - Nested dynstruct components go into `def.children`, rendered as `<c.children.Name />` without props in `view`.
  - No MobX in application code.
  - Reactive bindings: `bindProp` first, `bind(() => expr)` read-only, `bind(get, set)` for custom transformations.
  - Styling: Tailwind v4 with semantic design tokens via `className={tw('...')}`, zero hardcoded color literals.
  - MUI Theme Overrides: Forbidden in application/feature code. MUI `styleOverrides` exist exclusively in `@actdim/ui-core/theme/muiTheme.ts` as infrastructure bridges mapping MUI portal internals to semantic design tokens (`themeVar`).

## Document: docs/topic--adaptive-layout.md (Adaptive Layout and Back-Stack Navigation (LayoutService, BackStackService))

# Adaptive Layout and Back-Stack Navigation (LayoutService, BackStackService)

`@actdim/ui-core/layout` provides responsive screen tier classification, pointer detection, safe area inset propagation, and prioritized hardware/gesture Back-Stack management for Actdim applications.

---

## 1. Screen Tiers & Viewport Boundaries

The layout engine categorizes viewports into three semantic tiers, aligned with Tailwind v4 thresholds and Material UI breakpoints:

| Tier | Viewport Width | Description & UI Expectations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compact` | `< 768px` (under md) | Phone layout: single-column views, bottom navigation bar, full-screen dialogs, bottom sheets (`ActionSheet`). |
| `medium` | `768px - 1023px` (md to lg) | Tablet / foldable layout: compact multi-pane layouts, floating dialogs, side rails. |
| `expanded` | `>= 1024px` (lg and above) | Desktop layout: persistent sidebars, wide content containers, floating centered dialogs. |

### DOM Attributes and CSS Hooks

`LayoutService` automatically synchronizes the active layout with `document.documentElement` attributes:
- `data-tier="compact" | "medium" | "expanded"`: Enables tier-targeted CSS rules and Tailwind variant hooks (`compact:hidden`, `expanded:flex`).
- `data-pointer="coarse" | "fine"`: Reflects primary input capability (`(pointer: coarse)` vs `(pointer: fine)`). Used to enforce 44px minimum touch targets on mobile devices.
- `data-keyboard="visible"`: Set when the mobile virtual keyboard is active (detected via `window.visualViewport` height compression or text input focus on compact tier). Used to hide bottom navigation bars, floating buttons, and fixed bars that collide with the on-screen keyboard.

---

## 2. Safe Area Insets & CSS Custom Properties

`applySafeAreaToCssVariables` updates CSS custom properties on `:root` to ensure UI elements do not collide with notches, home indicator bars, or system status bars:

- `--safe-top`: Safe area inset top in pixels (default `0px`).
- `--safe-bottom`: Safe area inset bottom in pixels (default `0px`).
- `--safe-left`: Safe area inset left in pixels (default `0px`).
- `--safe-right`: Safe area inset right in pixels (default `0px`).
- `--toast-bottom-offset`: Dynamically computed bottom offset for toasts and floating action buttons (automatically set to `calc(var(--spacing-bottom-nav) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` on `compact` tier).

### Utility Classes

`@actdim/ui-core/theme.css` exports canonical Tailwind v4 utilities out of the box:
- `pt-safe`: `padding-top: max(env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), var(--safe-top, 0px))`
- `pb-safe`: `padding-bottom: max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px), var(--safe-bottom, 0px))`
- `pl-safe`: `padding-left: max(env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px), var(--safe-left, 0px))`
- `pr-safe`: `padding-right: max(env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px), var(--safe-right, 0px))`

---

## 3. Responsive Breakpoint Rules & Pitfalls

To prevent visual and behavioral desynchronization across devices, platforms, and embedded shells, follow these core architectural rules:

### 3.1. Layout-Shape vs Internal Density Invariant
- **Layout-Shape decisions** (showing/hiding toolbars, switching drawer vs header, bottom sheet vs dialog, 1-pane vs 2-pane) MUST use tier variants (`compact:`, `medium:`, `expanded:`) or reactive `m.tier`.
- **Viewport media queries (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`) are strictly forbidden for layout-shape or visibility toggles**:
  - Tailwind `sm:` (640px) falls inside `compact` (< 768px). A phone in landscape (e.g. 667x375 or 740x360) is `compact` in JS (`m.tier === 'compact'`). Using `sm:hidden` or `sm:flex` causes desktop-style controls to appear while menus remain bottom sheets.
  - Viewport queries measure `window.innerWidth`. If the app is embedded in a split view, webview shell, or side dock, container width != viewport width. `[data-tier]` always tracks the application's actual display tier.
- **Internal Density Permitted**: Tailwind breakpoints (`md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`) or Container Queries (`@container`) are permitted solely for fine-grained internal grid density (such as `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 lg:grid-cols-6`).

### 3.2. Landscape Mobile & Aspect Ratio Traps
- In landscape mode, smartphones present wide screens (667px - 932px) but severely constrained heights (360px - 430px).
- Fixed-height modals or non-scrollable sheets get clipped off-screen, hiding action buttons.
- Overlays on `compact` tier MUST enforce scrollable content bodies with dynamic viewport height limits: `max-h-[calc(100dvh-var(--safe-top)-var(--safe-bottom))] overflow-y-auto`.
- Toolbars on `compact` landscape should compress vertically (36px - 40px) to maximize content view area.

### 3.3. Virtual Keyboard Awareness
- On mobile devices, opening the on-screen keyboard compresses `visualViewport.height`.
- Fixed bottom navigation bars (`BottomNav`), floating action buttons (`Fab`), or sticky footers will float on top of the keyboard and obstruct form fields if not hidden.
- `LayoutService` synchronizes `data-keyboard="visible"` on `<html>` and updates `layout.keyboardVisible`.
- Bottom navigation bars and floating buttons must conditionally unmount when `m.keyboardVisible` is true or hide via CSS `data-keyboard:hidden`.

### 3.4. Safe Area Insets (Edge-to-Edge Displays)
- Hardcoded offsets (`pt-4`, `pb-4`, `bottom-0`, `top-0`) collide with camera notches, Dynamic Islands, and system gesture bars.
- Outermost layout boundaries and fixed bars must use `pt-safe`, `pb-safe`, `pl-safe`, `pr-safe` or `--safe-*` CSS custom properties.
- Floating overlays (toasts, FABs) must use `--toast-bottom-offset` on `compact` tier to clear the bottom navigation bar and home indicator.

### 3.5. Touch Targets & Sticky Hover
- When `data-pointer="coarse"` is active, interactive elements must meet the minimum touch target size of 44x44px (`min-h-touch`, `min-w-touch` or padding around icon buttons).
- Raw `:hover` pseudo-classes stick on touch devices after a tap. Use `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` or pointer variants so buttons do not remain visually highlighted.

### 3.6. Decision Matrix

| Context | Recommended Mechanism | Forbidden Anti-Pattern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show/hide actions or buttons | `compact:hidden`, `medium:inline-flex`, `m.tier` | `sm:hidden`, `hidden sm:flex` |
| Paradigm shift (sheet vs modal, drawer vs sidebar) | `m.tier === 'compact'` | CSS `@media` queries |
| Content grid column counts | `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4` or `@container` | Fixed pixel widths `w-[800px]` |
| Modal overlay height | `max-h-[calc(100dvh-...)] overflow-y-auto` | Fixed `h-[500px]` without scroll |
| Fixed bottom bars / FABs | `pb-safe`, hide when `keyboardVisible` | `bottom: 0; pb-2` |
| Touch button sizing | `min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` on coarse | Dense `< 36px` touch targets |
| Hover styles | `@media (hover: hover)` | Raw `:hover` sticking on touch |

---

## 4. LayoutService Architecture

`LayoutService` is a Dynstruct service managing viewport resizing, orientation, pointer detection, and virtual keyboard state:

### Public API

- `getCurrentLayout()`: Synchronously returns the cached `LayoutInfo` `{ tier, pointer, orientation, safeArea, keyboardVisible }`.
- `resolveCurrentLayout()`: Evaluates `window.innerWidth`, media queries, platform safe area insets, and `visualViewport` to produce fresh `LayoutInfo`.
- `applyLayoutAttributesToHtml(layout)`: Updates `data-tier`, `data-pointer`, and `data-keyboard` on `document.documentElement`.
- `applySafeAreaToCssVariables(insets)`: Injects `--safe-*` variables into `:root`.
- `initLayoutService(msgBus)`: Wires `window.resize`, `matchMedia`, `visualViewport`, and focus listeners, updating HTML attributes and publishing layout updates.

### MsgMesh Event Contracts

- `APP.LAYOUT.CHANGED`: Broadcast channel (`out`) published when screen tier, pointer kind, orientation, or safe area changes.
- `APP.LAYOUT.SET_SAFE_AREA`: Request channel (`in`) allowing host shells (e.g. MAUI mobile shell) to push updated device safe area insets into the web layer.

---

## 5. BackStackService & Prioritized Navigation

Mobile platforms (Android hardware Back button, iOS swipe-to-back, MAUI bridge) and desktop environments (Escape key) require predictable modal dismissal before page navigation. `BackStackService` provides a priority-ordered handler queue.

### Priority Queue Contract

Handlers are executed in descending order of `priority`. If a handler returns `true`, execution stops (the back event was handled). If it returns `false`, execution cascades down to the next handler.

| Component / Layer | Recommended Priority | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context menus & dropdowns (`AdaptiveMenu`) | `300` | Closes active menu popup. |
| Modal dialogs (`AdaptiveDialog`, `ActionSheet`) | `100` | Dismisses overlay (`open = false`). |
| In-page selection / search modes | `50` | Clears selection or search filter. |
| Root unhandled back handler | `0` (or fallback) | Navigates history backward or requests app minimization. |

### Registration & Lifecycle

- `registerBackHandler(handler)`: Queues a handler `{ id, priority, handle }`. Safe to call before MsgMesh is initialized.
- `unregisterBackHandler(id)`: Removes a registered handler. Overlays unregister in `onClose` and `onDestroy`.
- `setUnhandledBackHandler(fn)`: Configures the final fallback action when no queued handler handles the back event.

### MsgMesh Channels

- `APP.HOST.BACK`: Triggered by native shell bridge or browser Escape event. Dispatches to top-priority back handler.
- `APP.NAV.BACK`: Application navigation back command.
- `APP.NAV.CAN_GO_BACK`: Broadcasts whether any back handler or history step is available.

---

## Document: docs/topic--adaptive-overlays.md (Adaptive Overlays (AdaptiveDialog, ActionSheet, AdaptiveMenu))

# Adaptive Overlays (AdaptiveDialog, ActionSheet, AdaptiveMenu)

`@actdim/ui-core/components` provides responsive, platform-adaptive modal and overlay components:
- `AdaptiveDialog`: Full-screen modal with sticky header on compact devices; centered dialog on medium and expanded viewports.
- `ActionSheet`: Bottom-sheet drawer optimized for touch and mobile tiers with drag gestures and accessible action lists.
- `AdaptiveMenu`: Responsive context and action menu rendering an `ActionSheet` on mobile and a positioned desktop `Menu` on larger screens.

---

## 1. Core Principles

1. **Declared as children of the host component**:
   Overlays are defined inside `def.children` via their hook constructor (`useAdaptiveDialog`, `useActionSheet`, `useAdaptiveMenu`) and rendered in `view` as `<c.children.OverlayName />` without props or inline event handlers in JSX.

2. **Self-closing and Two-Way Binding**:
   Overlays dismiss themselves internally upon backdrop click, close button tap, or Escape key. The host manages and observes visibility through a two-way binding on `open`:
   - `bindProp(() => m, 'isDialogOpen')` for direct model synchronization.
   - `bind(get, set)` when dismissal triggers custom cleanup logic (e.g. resetting anchor element).

3. **Standard `onClose?: () => void` Contract**:
   In addition to two-way `open` synchronization, overlay components accept an optional `onClose` callback in `def.props` to allow host components to execute side effects upon dismissal.

4. **Hardware Back Button Handling**:
   All adaptive overlay components automatically register a hardware Back button / Escape handler (`registerBackHandler`) with prioritized execution while `open` is `true`. Handlers are cleanly deregistered when closed or on component destruction (`events.onDestroy`).

5. **Live Content via Fragment Children**:
   Overlay bodies, headers, and actions are passed using reactive bindings (`bind(() => <c.children.DialogBody />)`) referencing host fragment children (`React.FC`). This guarantees live reactivity without stale closures.

---

## 2. Component Reference

### AdaptiveDialog
- **Props**:
  - `open: boolean`
  - `onClose?: () => void`
  - `title?: React.ReactNode`
  - `subtitle?: React.ReactNode`
  - `tier?: LayoutTier` (defaults to current layout tier)
  - `fullScreen?: boolean`
  - `maxWidth?: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | false`
  - `fullWidth?: boolean`
  - `children?: React.ReactNode`
  - `actions?: React.ReactNode`
  - `primaryAction?: React.ReactNode`
  - `contentClassName?: TwClasses`
  - `paperClassName?: TwClasses`
  - `backHandlerPriority?: number` (default: 100)
  - `backHandlerId?: string`

### ActionSheet
- **Props**:
  - `open: boolean`
  - `onClose?: () => void`
  - `title?: string`
  - `actions: MenuItemAction[]`

### AdaptiveMenu
- **Props**:
  - `open: boolean`
  - `onClose?: () => void`
  - `tier: LayoutTier`
  - `anchorEl?: HTMLElement | null`
  - `anchorPosition?: { top: number; left: number }`
  - `title?: string`
  - `actions: MenuItemAction[]`

## Transitive Dependency Guidelines & Invariants

No exported invariants detected across repository dependencies.

## Custom Project Dependency Hooks (`.along/scripts/dep_scan.py`)

While Along natively auto-discovers dependencies across Node.js (`package.json`), Python (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`), .NET NuGet (`*.csproj`), Rust (`Cargo.toml`), and Go (`go.mod`), repositories using other ecosystems or internal package managers can supply a custom discovery hook:

- **Hook Path**: `.along/scripts/dep_scan.py` (or `scan_deps.py`).
- **Invocation**: `/along-dep-scan` or `along dep-scan` executes the script passing `--json` with working directory set to the project root.
- **Output Schema**: The script must write a JSON list to stdout:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "package": "custom-package",
      "ecosystem": "hex",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "files": [
        {
          "filename": "AGENTS.md",
          "path": "deps/custom-package/AGENTS.md"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
  ```
- **Monorepo Localization**: In multi-package repositories or submodules, subproject-specific hooks placed in `packages/<subproject>/.along/scripts/dep_scan.py` are executed automatically when scanning that subproject.

## Usage in Agent Sessions
When working on features involving any of the modules or external libraries above:
1. **Internal Submodules**: Follow conventions in the nearest `AGENTS.md` or subproject `docs/`.
2. **Third-Party Libraries**: Read the linked instruction files directly for framework-specific patterns and best practices.

## Document: docs/topic--developer-guide.md (@actdim/ui-core Developer & Consumer Integration Guide)

# @actdim/ui-core Developer & Consumer Integration Guide

`@actdim/ui-core` is the platform foundation package providing semantic design tokens, Tailwind v4 styling integration, Dynstruct component conventions, adaptive overlays, and layout services for Actdim applications.

This guide explains how any application consumes `@actdim/ui-core`, how to configure Tailwind v4, how to use `tw()` and components, how to safely extend the theme, and how to migrate an existing repository to `@actdim/ui-core`.

---

## 1. Prerequisites & Package Installation

### Package Installation
Install `@actdim/ui-core` via your package manager:

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/ui-core
# or
npm install @actdim/ui-core
```

For monorepos using pnpm workspaces, use the workspace protocol:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@actdim/ui-core": "workspace:*"
  }
}
```

### Peer Dependencies
`@actdim/ui-core` relies on the following peer dependencies:
- `@actdim/dynstruct` (`>=1.9.0`): Component model and reactivity.
- `@actdim/msgmesh` (`>=1.9.0`): Typed event bus and messaging.
- `@mui/material` (`>=9.0.1`), `@emotion/react`, `@emotion/styled`: Headless accessibility and portal primitives.
- `react` (`>=19.2.0`), `react-dom` (`>=19.2.0`): React 19 runtime.
- `tailwindcss` (`>=4.0.0`): Tailwind CSS v4 styling engine.

---

## 2. CSS & Tailwind v4 Integration

### CSS Entrypoint Setup
In your application CSS entrypoint (for example, `src/global.css`), import Tailwind v4 and the `@actdim/ui-core` token stylesheet:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@actdim/ui-core/theme.css';
```

### How Tokens Work in Tailwind v4
1. **Emitted on `:root`**: All tokens are declared in `@theme static` blocks inside `theme.css`. Tailwind emits all variables directly on `:root`.
2. **16 Semantic Scales**: Surface (backgrounds), Foreground (text/icons), Line (borders), Intent (primary/danger/success), Spacing, Object size, Container width, Text style, Emphasis, Font family, Line thickness, Corners, Elevation, Layer (zIndex), Motion, and State opacity.
3. **Automatic Dark Mode**: Mode colors switch automatically under `.dark` selectors. Never use `dark:` class prefixes in application JSX; use semantic tokens like `text-fg-muted` or `bg-surface-panel`.
4. **Responsive Tier Overrides**: Surface paddings and densities adapt automatically under `[data-tier="compact"]`.

---

## 3. Component Conventions & tw() Usage

### Dynstruct Component Model
All application UI elements must follow the Dynstruct component model:
1. **Struct + Def + Hook**: Every component defines a `ComponentStruct`, `ComponentDef`, and hook-constructor (`useXxx`).
2. **Prop-less JSX**: Child components are declared inside `def.children` and rendered as `<c.children.Name />`.
3. **Bus-First Communication**: Inter-component navigation and coordination must use MsgMesh channels (`c.msgBus.send`, `msgBroker.subscribe`). Never pass callback props (`onSelect`, `onNavigate`) across feature boundaries in JSX.
4. **Hooks Policy**: Standard state belongs in model `props: { ... }`. Built-in React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`) are prohibited in typical components; any non-typical usage requires an explicit `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports -- <reason>`.

### The tw() Class Helper
Application markup styles elements exclusively with semantic token classes through `tw()`:

```tsx
import { tw } from '@/theme/tw';

<div className={tw('flex items-center gap-snug p-normal bg-surface-panel rounded-panel')} />
```

- **Compile-Time Checking**: TypeScript validates every token class in string literals against `TwClasses`. Raw numeric classes (`p-4`, `text-slate-500`, `rounded-lg`) produce compile errors.
- **Runtime Merging**: Merges classes safely via `clsx` and token-aware `tailwind-merge`.
- **Content-Only Exception**: `mergeClasses(...)` is reserved strictly for non-UI content palettes (e.g. syntax highlighting, reader themes).

---

## 4. Adaptive Overlays & Layout Services

### Adaptive Overlays
Use canonical primitives from `@actdim/ui-core/components`:
- `AdaptiveDialog`: Adapts from a centered dialog on expanded desktop to a full-screen or bottom sheet on compact mobile.
- `ActionSheet`: Slide-up mobile sheet with backdrop scrim.
- `AdaptiveMenu`: Context/dropdown menu positioned relative to target or anchored bottom.

**Two-Way Binding Invariant**: Overlays bind open state via `bindProp(() => m, 'isDialogOpen')`. Callback props (`onOpen`, `onClose`) in JSX are forbidden.

### Layout & Back-Stack Navigation
- **Layout Tiers**: Managed by `LayoutService` (`@actdim/ui-core/layout`). Automatically applies `data-tier="compact" | "medium" | "expanded"` to the `<html>` root.
- **Safe Areas**: Safe area insets are synced to CSS custom properties (`--safe-top`, `--safe-bottom`, `--safe-left`, `--safe-right`).
- **Hardware Back Button**: Managed by `BackStackService` (`@actdim/ui-core/layout`). The topmost open overlay is dismissed first on Android/browser back navigation.

---

## 5. Theme Extension Policy

### Centralization Invariant
All core UI tokens (palettes, spacing scales, standard radii, z-indices) are centralized in `@actdim/ui-core`. An application must NEVER monkey-patch or redefine standard UI tokens in its own stylesheets.

### Permitted Application Extensions
Applications frequently require domain-specific styles, layout geometries, or icon libraries. These are legal and must be declared as follows:

1. **Third-Party Tailwind Plugins in Application CSS**:
   Applications may register supplementary plugins in their root CSS (e.g. `src/global.css`):
   ```css
   @plugin '@tailwindcss/typography';
   @plugin 'tailwindcss-animate';
   @plugin '@iconify/tailwind4' {
       prefixes: mdi, tabler, material-symbols, ph, devicon, logos;
   }
   ```

2. **Application Layout Utilities (@utility)**:
   Layout utilities specific to the application shell belong in the application CSS:
   ```css
   @utility h-app {
       height: calc(100dvh - var(--spacing-header));
   }
   @utility wco-header {
       padding-top: max(env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), var(--safe-top, 0px));
       padding-left: max(1rem, env(titlebar-area-x, 0px), env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px));
   }
   @utility pt-safe {
       padding-top: max(env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), var(--safe-top, 0px));
   }
   ```

3. **Application-Specific CSS Variables**:
   Variables for application layout offsets are declared on `:root` or container attributes in application CSS:
   ```css
   :root {
       --toast-bottom-offset: 0px;
   }
   [data-tier="compact"], [data-tier="compact"] * {
       --toast-bottom-offset: calc(var(--spacing-bottom-nav) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
   }
   ```

4. **App Token Layer (Replacing Domain Constants for New Code)**:
   For domain-specific colors that are not part of core UI chrome (e.g. ebook sepia reader page background, syntax highlighting), declare them in the app token layer (`src/theme/app-theme.css`) under `@theme static` and combine them via `createThemeKit(appThemeTokens)`. This gives app tokens full compile-time `tw()` validation alongside core tokens, replacing legacy domain constants for new code. For non-token dynamic classes or external libraries, merge with `mergeClasses(...)`.

5. **Package Consumer Setup and Optional Peers**:
   - Consumers import `@actdim/ui-core/theme.css` in their root CSS (e.g. `src/global.css`).
   - `theme.css` includes `@source "../../dist/components";` (and fallback `@source "../components";`) so Tailwind v4 automatically discovers classes used by ui-core components even if consumers use atypical folder layouts.
   - `@actdim/dynstruct-mui` and `vite` are marked as optional peer dependencies (`peerDependenciesMeta.*.optional: true`). Non-MUI consumers or build tools other than Vite can consume `@actdim/ui-core` without installing unneeded packages.

---

## 6. Project Migration & Adoption Walkthrough

When migrating an existing project to `@actdim/ui-core`, follow this standard procedure:

### Step 1: Install Package & Register Dependency
Install `@actdim/ui-core` and execute Along dependency registration:
```bash
pnpm add @actdim/ui-core
along dep-scan --link
```
Verify that `docs/topic--dependencies.md` links to `node_modules/@actdim/ui-core/llms.txt`.

### Step 2: Set Up 1-Liner Code Bridges
To avoid rewriting hundreds of imports across an existing application, create lean re-export bridges:

- `src/theme/tw.ts`:
  ```typescript
  export * from '@actdim/ui-core/theme';
  ```
- `src/config/muiTheme.ts`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      muiBreakpoints,
      createMuiAppTheme,
      defaultMuiTheme,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/theme';
  ```
- `src/components/core/AdaptiveDialog.tsx`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      type AdaptiveDialogProps,
      type AdaptiveDialogStruct,
      useAdaptiveDialog,
      AdaptiveDialog,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/components';
  ```
- `src/components/core/ActionSheet.tsx`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      type ActionSheetProps,
      type ActionSheetStruct,
      useActionSheet,
      ActionSheet,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/components';
  ```
- `src/components/core/AdaptiveMenu.tsx`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      type AdaptiveMenuProps,
      type AdaptiveMenuStruct,
      useAdaptiveMenu,
      AdaptiveMenu,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/components';
  ```
- `src/services/LayoutService.tsx`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      getCurrentLayout,
      resolveCurrentLayout,
      applyLayoutAttributesToHtml,
      applySafeAreaToCssVariables,
      initLayoutService,
      useLayoutService,
      LayoutService,
      type LayoutServiceStruct,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/layout';
  ```
- `src/services/BackStackService.tsx`:
  ```typescript
  export {
      backStack,
      useBackStack,
      type BackStackItem,
      type BackStackServiceStruct,
      type BackStackHandler,
      type BackStackOptions,
  } from '@actdim/ui-core/layout';
  ```

### Step 3: Clean-Room Documentation Purge
Remove duplicate copies of UI guidelines to prevent slug collisions in Along:
```bash
git rm docs/topic--frontend-conventions.md
git rm docs/topic--theme-tokens.md
```
Never leave 10-line stubs. The slugs `frontend-conventions` and `theme-tokens` belong exclusively to `@actdim/ui-core`.

### Step 4: Streamline AGENTS.md
In the application's `AGENTS.md`, remove all verbose lists of tokens, MobX bans, and overlay mechanics. Replace them with the canonical 2-line pointer:

```markdown
- **UI & Frontend Invariants**: All UI guidelines, component models, design tokens, adaptive layout tiers, and overlay rules are governed exclusively by `@actdim/ui-core` (`node_modules/@actdim/ui-core/docs/INDEX.md`). Application-specific architecture is defined in `docs/topic--architecture.md`.
```

### Step 5: Document the Application Delta
In `docs/topic--architecture.md`, add a concise section documenting ONLY the application's configuration delta:
- Core tokens from `@actdim/ui-core` via `tw()`.
- Application-specific plugins (e.g. Iconify, Typography).
- Application-specific layout utilities and CSS variables.
- Link to `@actdim/ui-core/docs/topic--developer-guide.md`.

---

Before completing adoption, execute these verification commands:

1. **Negative Assertions**:
   - Verify `Test-Path docs/topic--frontend-conventions.md` is `False`.
   - Verify `Test-Path docs/topic--theme-tokens.md` is `False`.
   - Verify `AGENTS.md` contains 0 redundant token scales or MobX mentions.

   - Run `along test`: 100% test pass rate.
4. **Knowledge Base Compilation**:
   - Run `along kb-sync`: 0 broken relative Markdown links.

## Document: docs/topic--frontend-conventions.md (Frontend Coding Conventions (Dynstruct + MsgMesh))

# Frontend Coding Conventions (Dynstruct + MsgMesh)

Standard architectural and coding conventions for applications and packages built on `@actdim/ui-core`, `@actdim/dynstruct`, and `@actdim/msgmesh`.

---

## 1. Component Model

1. **Every UI element is a Dynstruct component** (`@actdim/dynstruct`): `ComponentStruct` + `ComponentDef` + `useComponent` + `toReact`. See [Dynstruct Documentation](../../dynstruct/docs/INDEX.md).
2. **Public vs. internal struct** (`ComponentStructExt<PublicStruct, InternalState>`):
   - Public `ComponentStruct`: only props passed by parents and the public `msgScope`. No loading flags, caches, or internal indices.
   - Internal state: private reactive `props`, private `actions`, private `effects`.
3. **Self-documenting `msgScope`**: the struct explicitly defines the component bus contract:
   - `provide` - channels the component serves (`msgBroker.provide`).
   - `subscribe` - channels/events it listens to (`msgBroker.subscribe`).
   - `publish` - channels it sends to or requests from (`c.msgBus.send`, `c.msgBus.request`).
4. **Children, not inline JSX**: nested dynstruct components (including `@actdim/dynstruct-mui` wrappers) go into `def.children` via their `useXxx` constructor and render as `<c.children.Name />`.
5. **Bindings**: `bindProp(() => m, 'prop')` for two-way binding; `bind(() => expr)` for read-only values; `bind(get, set)` only for custom getter/setter logic.
6. **Params semantics**: plain params are initial values (applied once by `useComponent`); live input goes only through bindings. Never read `params.x` in a hook-constructor (`def.props` holds defaults only; live values for children come from `m` via `bindProp` / `bind`); bind factory-child props per value (`bind(() => p.item)`), never pass `p` whole.
7. **Clean prop-less JSX and callback policy**: Dynstruct views must remain prop-free in JSX (`<c.children.Name />`). Never pass callback functions or event handlers as JSX attributes. Callback props are strictly prohibited for inter-component coordination across features and pages (e.g. `onSelect*`, `onNavigate*`); cross-component communication and user intents must go through typed MsgMesh channels (`c.msgBus.send`, `msgBroker.subscribe`), and open/close state through two-way bindings (`bindProp`). Low-level event handlers (`onClick`, `onClose`, `onChange`) are permitted exclusively on primitive wrappers (such as `@actdim/dynstruct-mui` controls) when wired inside `def.children` during hook initialization.

---

## 2. State, Lifecycle & Reactivity

1. **Dynstruct-first lifecycle**:
   - State -> `props: { ... }`, mutate via `m.prop = value`.
   - Mount / unmount -> `events: { onReady, onInit, onDestroy, onCatch, onValidate }`. Async loading on mount goes into `events.onReady`.
   - Side effects -> `effects: { ... }` (auto-tracks accessed model props).
   - Callbacks -> `actions: { ... }`.
   - Form inputs -> `c.mapToEdit('fieldPath')`.
2. **Hooks Policy (Dynstruct-First, Not a Ban)**:
   - Built-in React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useLayoutEffect`, `useReducer`, `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `useRef`) are not needed in typical components. Use reactive model properties, lifecycle events, and actions instead.
   - A built-in hook is acceptable only for non-typical cases the component model does not cover. Because ESLint warns on them (`@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports`), mark a justified use with `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports -- <reason>`.
   - Custom and third-party hooks (own `useXxx`, external library hooks, React context providers) are permitted inside Dynstruct components as long as app-visible state lives in the model and communication goes through bindings and MsgMesh. See [Dynstruct React Integration](../../dynstruct/docs/topic--04-react-integration.md).
3. **No direct MobX in application code**: no imports from `mobx` / `mobx-react-lite` (`runInAction`, `action`, `observable`, `makeObservable`, `makeAutoObservable`, `observer`, `useLocalObservable`). Dynstruct encapsulates reactivity: mutate model props directly (`m.foo = bar`) or through `actions`.
4. **Reactivity granularity** (`ComponentProp.reactive?: true | false | 'shallow'`):
   - `'shallow'` - for large collections, file trees, read-only arrays: container mutations are tracked, items are not proxied.
   - `false` - for static configuration.

---

## 3. Communication (@actdim/msgmesh)

1. **Bus-first**: inter-component interaction, notifications, and navigation go through `c.msgBus`. No prop drilling across features, no cross-component ref mutation. See [MsgMesh Documentation](../../msgmesh/docs/INDEX.md).
2. **Channel groups**:
   - `in` - request payloads for request/response calls (`c.msgBus.request({ channel, group: 'in' })`).
   - `out` - provider responses and broadcast events (`msgBroker.subscribe`).
   - `ex` - fire-and-forget commands.
3. **Payloads through `c.msgBus`** are normalized (observables -> plain values); class instances (`File`, `Blob`, `Date`) are passed by reference.
4. **Route navigation controls are links**: a control whose action is "go to a route" renders a real `<a href>` so
   middle-click, Ctrl/Cmd+click and "open in new tab" work. Use `href` on dynstruct-mui `Button` / `IconButton` /
   list and menu items, `href` on `MenuItemAction` (`AdaptiveMenu`, `ActionSheet`), `NavLink` or
   `createNavLinkClick(c.msgBus, href)` on a plain `<a>` (`@actdim/dynstruct/services/react/NavLink`). A plain left
   click is intercepted and sent as `APP.NAV.GOTO {url}` (no reload); modified and middle clicks are left to the
   browser. Side effects of an in-place navigation (closing a dialog or drawer) go into `onNavigate`.
   Programmatic `APP.NAV.GOTO` stays for URL-state sync, redirects (auth, after save) and non-control flows.

---

## 4. TypeScript & Syntax Guidelines

1. **Control flow blocks**: Always use multi-line `{ ... }` blocks for all control flow (`if`, `for`, `while`, `else`). Single-line bodies without braces are strictly prohibited.
2. **Type definition integrity**: Use `type` exclusively. Never use `interface` or `class`.
3. **Design Tokens**: All styling must use semantic tokens via `className={tw('...')}`. Hardcoded hex/rgb/color names are strictly prohibited. See [Theme Tokens Guide](./topic--theme-tokens.md).
4. **MUI Theme Overrides Boundary**: Application and feature code must never declare or customize MUI `styleOverrides`. MUI is used strictly as a behavioral/accessibility foundation wrapped in Dynstruct components. All theme overrides for portal containers (`Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Popover`, `Backdrop`) belong exclusively in `@actdim/ui-core/src/theme/muiTheme.ts` to bridge MUI internals to semantic design tokens (`themeVar`).
5. **Responsive Tier Variants vs Breakpoints**: Visibility, toolbar composition, and structural layout branching must use `compact:`, `medium:`, `expanded:` or `m.tier`. Raw Tailwind `sm:` visibility toggles (`sm:hidden`, `sm:flex`) are strictly prohibited because `sm:` (640px) triggers on landscape phones while `m.tier` remains `compact`. Safe area padding (`pt-safe`, `pb-safe`, `pl-safe`, `pr-safe`), keyboard awareness (`data-keyboard="visible"` / `m.keyboardVisible`), touch target minimums (44x44px for `data-pointer="coarse"`), sticky hover prevention (`@media (hover: hover)`), and BackStack navigation queues are provided and governed by `@actdim/ui-core/layout` and `theme.css`. See [Adaptive Layout Guide](./topic--adaptive-layout.md).

---

## 5. Internationalization Invariants (@actdim/ui-core/i18n)

1. **No user-visible literals in JSX**: Hardcoded user-visible string literals in JSX, templates, or component state are strictly prohibited. All UI text must use translation keys via `useT('<ns>')` or `MessageDescriptor` (`{ key, params, fallback }`). See [UI Internationalization Guide](./topic--i18n.md).
2. **No ad-hoc toLocaleString or unmemoized Intl**: Never use `Date.prototype.toLocaleString`, `toLocaleDateString`, `Number.prototype.toLocaleString`, or ad-hoc `Intl.*` constructors in features. Use the centralized memoized formatters from `@actdim/ui-core/i18n` (`formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, `formatNumber`, `formatBytes`, `formatDuration`, `formatRelative`, `formatList`).
3. **UI Locale Separation**: Application UI language (`APP.LOCALE.*`) is strictly separated from content, study, and media languages.
4. **Server Display Text Ban**: Backend APIs must never return human-facing display text as their contract. Servers return `errorCode` and `params`; client applications map error codes to localized messages.

---

## Related Context

- [Knowledge Base Index](./INDEX.md)
- [UI Internationalization Foundation](./topic--i18n.md)
- [Theme Tokens and tw() Class Helper](./topic--theme-tokens.md)
- [Adaptive Overlays Guide](./topic--adaptive-overlays.md)
- [Adaptive Layout and Back-Stack Navigation](./topic--adaptive-layout.md)
- [Dynstruct Knowledge Base](../../dynstruct/docs/INDEX.md)
- [MsgMesh Knowledge Base](../../msgmesh/docs/INDEX.md)

---

## Document: docs/topic--i18n.md (UI Internationalization Foundation (@actdim/ui-core/i18n))

# UI Internationalization Foundation (@actdim/ui-core/i18n)

The `@actdim/ui-core/i18n` package provides the centralized, reactive internationalization foundation for Actdim applications. It encapsulates `i18next` behind typed MsgMesh contracts, offers React hooks for live language switching, and includes memoized Intl-based formatting helpers.

---

## 1. Architecture & Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    APP["App Startup (main.tsx)"]
    SVC["initLocaleService(msgBus, options)"]
    BUS["MsgMesh Bus ('APP.LOCALE.*')"]
    HOOK["useT('<ns>') in Components"]
    RUNTIME["i18next Runtime Engine"]
    RESOURCES["Centralized JSON Resources"]

    APP --> SVC
    SVC --> RUNTIME
    SVC --> BUS
    BUS -.->|APP.LOCALE.CHANGED| HOOK
    BUS -.->|APP.LOCALE.SET_PREFERENCE| SVC
    HOOK --> RUNTIME
    RUNTIME --> RESOURCES
```

### Runtime Lifecycle
1. `initLocaleService(msgBus, options)` is awaited before the initial application render.
2. The service resolves the active locale in strict order:
   `user preference` > `stored preference` > `host locale (MAUI)` > `navigator languages` > `fallback locale`.
3. Boot namespaces (`ui-core` and app boot namespaces) are loaded.
4. `<html lang dir>` attributes are synchronized on `document.documentElement`.
5. An `APP.LOCALE.CHANGED` message is dispatched on the bus.
6. When `APP.LOCALE.SET_PREFERENCE` is received, missing namespaces for the target locale are loaded first before switching the runtime language, preventing flashes of untranslated keys.

---

## 2. Key Naming & Resource Structure

All translations follow a strict semantic hierarchy:

```text
<ns>.<area>.<item>
```

- `<ns>`: Namespace name corresponding to the JSON file name (e.g. `ui-core`, `common`, `auth`, `media`).
- `<area>`: Screen, component, or semantic subdomain (e.g. `dialog`, `menu`, `login`).
- `<item>`: Specific text element in camelCase (e.g. `cancelButton`, `title`, `confirmPassword`).

### Resource File Layout

Resources are centralized at package or application level and never colocated inside feature subfolders:

```text
src/locales/
  en/
    ui-core.json
    common.json
  ru/
    ui-core.json
    common.json
```

---

## 3. MessageDescriptor Pattern

For components, models, and async error handlers that store or pass text references before rendering, use `MessageDescriptor`:

```typescript
export type MessageDescriptor = {
    key: string;
    params?: Record<string, unknown>;
    fallback?: string;
};
```

`AdaptiveDialog`, `AdaptiveMenu`, and `ActionSheet` accept both string literals and `MessageDescriptor` objects for titles, subtitles, and action labels.

To resolve a descriptor into a translated string at render time:

```typescript
import { translate } from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';

const text = translate({
    key: 'ui-core:dialog.close',
    fallback: 'Close',
});
```

---

## 4. React Integration (useT and createTypedT)

Components consume translations via `useT`:

```typescript
import { useT } from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';

export const MyComponent = () => {
    const t = useT('ui-core');

    return (
        <button type="button">
            {t('dialog.close')}
        </button>
    );
};
```

When the active locale changes via `APP.LOCALE.SET_PREFERENCE`, components using `useT` or `useLocale` re-render automatically via `useSyncExternalStore`.

### Strongly Typed Keys

Applications derive strictly type-checked translation hooks using `createTypedT`:

```typescript
import { createTypedT } from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';
import type enResources from '@/locales/en';

export const useAppT = createTypedT<typeof enResources>();

// In a component:
const t = useAppT('common');
t('confirm'); // Type-checked: typos produce compile-time errors!
```

Do not annotate the hook type explicitly; let TypeScript infer `UseTypedT<TResources>` from `createTypedT`.

When passing `t` to helper functions or component props, use the exported `TypedT` type:

```typescript
import type { TypedT } from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';
import type enResources from '@/locales/en';

export function formatPageTitle(t: TypedT<typeof enResources, 'pages'>): string {
    return t('header.title');
}
```

Plural keys are called by their base key (`t('items', { count })`), and `TranslationKey` automatically accepts the base key when `_zero`, `_one`, `_two`, `_few`, `_many`, or `_other` variants exist.

### In dynstruct components

In dynstruct components, `t()` (and formatters like `formatNumber`, `formatDate`) is reactive inside `view`, bindings (`bind(() => t(...))`), computed property getters, and effects. It automatically registers a dependency on the i18n runtime revision via `fromExternalStore`:

```typescript
import { t } from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';
import { bind } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/core';

// In def:
view: () => <span>{t('common.save')}</span>,
children: {
    child: useChild({
        label: bind(() => t('common.cancel')), // Follows language changes live
    }),
},
```

A `t()` result passed as a plain parameter to a hook-constructor (e.g. `label: t('common.cancel')`) or stored as a static prop default is frozen at creation time. Always wrap translated parameters with `bind(() => t(...))` or translate in `view` / computed getters.

Plain React components continue using `useT` and `useLocale`.

---

## 5. Formatters

All date, time, number, byte, and duration formatting must use the centralized formatters instead of ad-hoc JavaScript helpers:

```typescript
import {
    formatDate,
    formatDateTime,
    formatNumber,
    formatBytes,
    formatDuration,
    formatRelative,
    formatList,
} from '@actdim/ui-core/i18n';

// Dates and numbers
formatDate(new Date()); // "10/21/2026" (en) or "21.10.2026" (ru)
formatDateTime(new Date()); // "10/21/2026, 03:30 PM"
formatNumber(1250000); // "1,250,000" (en) or "1 250 000" (ru)

// Storage and duration
formatBytes(1572864); // "1.5 MB" (en) or "1,5 МБ" (ru)
formatDuration(3660, { style: 'short' }); // "1 hr 1 min" (en) or "1 ч 1 мин" (ru)
formatDuration(7200, { style: 'long' }); // "2 hours" (en) or "2 часа" (ru)

// Relative time and lists
formatRelative(-1, 'day'); // "yesterday" (en) or "вчера" (ru)
formatList(['One', 'Two', 'Three']); // "One, Two, and Three"
```

All formatters automatically bind to the active application locale and memoize `Intl.*` formatter instances.

---

## 6. Server Error Codes Rule

The backend server never returns human-facing display text as its contract:
1. Backend responses carry a mandatory `errorCode` and optional `params` in `errorResponse`.
2. Client-side error classifiers map `errorCode` to a semantic translation key (e.g. `errors.codes.STORAGE_FULL`).
3. Raw error text from the server is strictly reserved for developer debugging logs and diagnostic overlays.

---

## 7. Adding a New Language

Adding support for an additional language requires no code changes:
1. Create a new directory under `src/locales/<locale-code>/` (e.g. `src/locales/de/`).
2. Add corresponding JSON files with identical keys matching `en`.
3. Register the locale code in `supportedLocales` during `initLocaleService`.
4. Run `pnpm run i18n:check` to verify complete key parity.

---

## 8. Tooling & Linting

- **Key Parity Check**: Run `pnpm run i18n:check` (or `checkLocaleParity` from `@actdim/ui-core/i18n-tooling`) to verify that all translated files match the keys of the base `en` locale.
- **ESLint Rule**: `eslint-plugin-i18next` enforces `i18next/no-literal-string` in `jsx-text-only` mode across `src/components/**` to prevent untranslated text literals.

---

## Document: docs/topic--theme-tokens.md (Theme Tokens and the tw() Class Helper)

# Theme Tokens and the tw() Class Helper

All visual style values in Actdim applications (colors, spacing, sizes, typography, borders, corners,
shadows, layers, motion) are **semantic design tokens** declared once in
`src/theme/theme.css`. Markup never uses raw Tailwind values (`text-slate-500`, `p-4`,
`rounded-lg`); it uses token classes (`text-fg-muted`, `p-normal`, `rounded-control`) through the
typed `tw()` helper, which rejects anything else at compile time.

## Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/theme/theme.css` | Source of truth: every token with a description, `Based on` / `Replaces` per scale, a TOKEN TABLE, `.dark` and `[data-tier="compact"]` overrides, tier variants, `focus-ring` utility, `:focus-visible` base style. |
| `src/theme/theme.generated.ts` | Generated from theme.css: `themeTokens` (CSS variable, value, per-mode values, sub-properties), `themeUtilities`, `themeVariants`. Committed. Do not edit. |
| `src/theme/tooling/` | Token parsing, rendering, and generator engine (`parseTheme`, `renderTheme`, `generate`, `themeTokensPlugin`). Exported via `./theme-tooling`. |
| `src/theme/themeKit.ts` | Extensible theme kit factory (`createThemeKit`, `ThemeKit<T>`, `ThemeTokenSet`, `ScaleNames`). |
| `src/theme/themeChrome.ts` | Browser chrome meta colors (`themeChromeColors`: `#ffffff` light, `#0f172a` dark). |
| `src/theme/tw.ts` | `tw()`, `mergeClasses()`, `TwClasses`, scale types (`ThemeColor`, `ThemeSpacing`, ...), tailwind-merge config. |
| `src/theme/tw.typecheck.ts` | Compile-time tests of the class validation (run by `tsc -b`). |
| `src/theme/themeRuntime.ts` | Typed runtime contract for getting, setting, resetting, and batch applying CSS variables on `:root` or scoped elements (`themeRuntime`, `themeCssVars`). |
| `postcss.ts` | Thin CLI / PostCSS wrapper around `src/theme/tooling` (`pnpm theme:gen`). |
| `src/theme/muiTheme.ts` | MUI theme built from the same tokens (palette, radius, font, zIndex). |

## How tokens become classes

Tokens live in Tailwind 4 `@theme static` blocks, so they are plain `:root` CSS variables. The
variable prefix is a Tailwind namespace and decides which classes exist:

```css
@theme static {
    --spacing-normal: 0.75rem;      /* -> p-normal, gap-normal, mt-normal, ... */
    --color-fg-muted: #64748b;      /* -> text-fg-muted, border-fg-muted, ... */
    --radius-panel: 0.75rem;        /* -> rounded-panel, rounded-t-panel, ... */
}

.dark {
    --color-fg-muted: #94a3b8;      /* same class, other value: no dark: in markup */
}
```

## Scales

| Scale | Elements | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Surface (background) | page, panel, inset, popup, dialog, hover, selected, inverse, scrim | `bg-surface-panel` |
| Foreground (text, icons) | fg-default, fg-muted, fg-faint, fg-disabled, fg-inverse | `text-fg-muted` |
| Line (borders) | line-default, line-muted, line-strong, focus | `border-line-default` |
| Intent | primary, secondary, success, info, warning, danger, neutral; roles base / -strong / -soft / -line / -contrast | `bg-danger-soft text-danger-strong` |
| Spacing | micro, tight, snug, normal, relaxed, loose, spacious, vast | `gap-snug p-normal` |
| Object size | control-xs/sm/md/lg, icon-sm/md/lg, avatar-sm/md/lg, cover-sm/md, touch, header, bottom-nav, sidebar | `h-control-md` |
| Container width | form, dialog-sm/md/lg, popup, content, page (+ built-in prose) | `max-w-dialog-md` |
| Text style | micro, caption, label, body, body-lg, title, headline, display | `text-title` |
| Emphasis | regular, emphasis, strong | `font-emphasis` |
| Font family | ui, prose, code | `font-code` |
| Line thickness | thin, thick, heavy (border, ring, outline, divide) | `border-b-thick` |
| Corners | control, panel, popup, dialog (+ built-in full) | `rounded-panel` |
| Elevation | panel, popup, dialog (+ built-in none) | `shadow-popup` |
| Layer | sticky, header, drawer, dialog, popup, toast, tooltip (MUI zIndex values) | `z-dialog` |
| Motion | duration short/medium/long, ease standard/enter/exit | `duration-short ease-enter` |
| State opacity | disabled, muted | `opacity-disabled` |
| Variants | dark, compact, medium, expanded | `compact:hidden` |

## App Token Layer

Applications can extend core tokens without modifying `@actdim/ui-core`:

1. **Declare in App CSS**: Place domain or application tokens in an app CSS file (e.g. `src/theme/app-theme.css`) using `@theme static { ... }` blocks and optional mode overrides (`.dark`).
2. **Compile-Time Generator**: Use `themeTokensPlugin({ appCssFile, outFile })` from `@actdim/ui-core/theme-tooling` in `vite.config.ts`, or call `generateAppThemeTokens({ appCssFile, outFile })`.
3. **Additive Invariant**: App tokens are strictly additive. Redefining a core token without `allowCoreOverrides: true` throws an error. Defining mode overrides in `.dark` without a matching `@theme` token also throws an error.
4. **Typed Theme Kit**: Combine core and app tokens with `createThemeKit(appThemeTokens)` from `@actdim/ui-core/theme`. The returned `tw` validates both core and app classes with full IDE autocompletion and compile-time rejection.

## MUI Theme Integration and styleOverrides Architecture

MUI (`@mui/material`) is used exclusively for headless accessibility, portals, and low-level interactive primitives (dialogs, drawers, popovers, touch targets). It is NOT used as an application styling engine.

### Role of styleOverrides in ui-core

In `src/theme/muiTheme.ts`, `styleOverrides` serve as a one-time infrastructure bridge connecting internal MUI portal elements to semantic design tokens:

- **Portal DOM Containers**: Elements like `.MuiDialog-paper`, `.MuiDrawer-paper`, `.MuiPopover-paper`, and `.MuiBackdrop-root` render outside the standard DOM hierarchy via React portals. Their default Material Design aesthetics are replaced with design tokens via `themeVar(...)`:
  - `MuiBackdrop.root`: `themeVar('color', 'surface-scrim')`
  - `MuiDialog.paper`: `themeVar('color', 'surface-dialog')`, `themeVar('radius', 'dialog')`, `themeVar('shadow', 'dialog')`
  - `MuiDrawer.paper`: `themeVar('color', 'surface-dialog')`
  - `MuiPopover.paper`: `themeVar('color', 'surface-popup')`, `themeVar('radius', 'popup')`, `themeVar('shadow', 'popup')`
- **Touch Target Enforcements**: Mobile/touch accessibility minimums (`44px` on `pointer: coarse`) are enforced globally on `MuiButtonBase` and `MuiIconButton`.

### Strict Boundary and Negative Invariants

1. **No Application-Level styleOverrides**: Applications (`src/apps/*`) and feature modules must NEVER define or customize MUI `styleOverrides`. Applications import `createMuiAppTheme` from `@actdim/ui-core/theme` without mutation.
2. **Tailwind-First Styling**: All application UI styling is written with Dynstruct components and Tailwind v4 semantic token classes via `className={tw('...')}`.
3. **Infrastructure Isolation**: `styleOverrides` are an infrastructure adapter in `@actdim/ui-core`, not a template or standard for feature development. If a new primitive with portal DOM nodes is introduced to `@actdim/ui-core`, its token bindings belong strictly in `src/theme/muiTheme.ts`.

---

## ThemeService Architecture and Lifecycle

`ThemeService` (`src/theme/ThemeService.tsx`) coordinates theme preference, system dark mode queries, DOM attributes, browser chrome meta tags, and MsgMesh events.

### Mode and Preference Types

- `ThemePreference`: `'light' | 'dark' | 'system'` (user preference, persisted in `localStorage`).
- `ThemeMode`: `'light' | 'dark'` (resolved active mode applied to the document).

### Service Contracts

1. **System Resolution**: `resolveThemeMode(preference, systemMode)` resolves `'system'` to the current OS setting (`matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`).
2. **DOM Synchronization**:
   - `applyThemeToHtml(mode)`: Toggles class `.dark` on `document.documentElement` and sets `data-theme="dark" | "light"`.
   - `applyThemeToMeta(mode)`: Updates `<meta name="theme-color">` to match browser chrome color (`#ffffff` for light, `#0f172a` for dark via `themeChromeColors`).
3. **MsgMesh Integration**:
   - `APP.THEME.CHANGED`: Broadcasts `{ mode, preference, muiTheme }` to subscribed components (used by Dynstruct root to update MUI `ThemeProvider`).
   - `APP.THEME.SET_PREFERENCE`: Inbound command accepting `{ preference }`.

---

## IDE and Editor Integration (Tailwind CSS IntelliSense)

To enable class completions, linting, and hover previews (displaying generated CSS and variable values) for `tw('...')` calls inside VS Code:

### 1. Class Function Recognition
The Tailwind CSS IntelliSense extension (`bradlc.vscode-tailwindcss`) by default inspects only `class` and `className` JSX attributes. To parse class string arguments inside function calls like `tw('...')` or `clsx('...')`, add them to `tailwindCSS.classFunctions` in workspace `.vscode/settings.json`:

```json
{
    "tailwindCSS.classFunctions": ["tw", "clsx", "cva", "cn"]
}
```

### 2. Monorepo Config Resolution in Tailwind v4
In Tailwind v4, configuration is CSS-first (`@import 'tailwindcss';` + `@theme static`). In a monorepo where `@actdim/ui-core` is an extracted library package without a direct Tailwind runtime build, the language server needs to know which CSS stylesheet supplies the theme tokens and utilities:

```json
{
    "tailwindCSS.experimental.configFile": "src/apps/webapp/src/global.css"
}
```

Specifying `tailwindCSS.experimental.configFile` in the root `.vscode/settings.json` points the language server to `src/apps/webapp/src/global.css`, ensuring that hover styles and completions work across both application code and package components (such as `ActionSheet`, `AdaptiveDialog`, `AdaptiveMenu`).
